title: Cross-workload Quantization Profile Stress & Regression Detection
creator: Ava Chen
description: Build a repeatable stress and regression detection harness that evaluates FP16/INT8/INT4 quantization profiles across diverse production-like workloads. The goal is to quantify throughput (tokens/sec), tail latency (p95/p99), and quality trade-offs (embedding cosine, BLEU/ROUGE snapshots, hallucination rate) and to detect regressions automatically when model runtime or quantization changes are introduced. This ticket covers harness design, metric definition, regression thresholds, synthetic/trace workloads, statistical test selection, and alerting/rollback runbook.
acceptance_criteria: A harness that can run nightly jobs covering 6 workload buckets (short-chat, long-form, instruction, code-gen, summarization, search-relevance) and produce deterministic metric outputs
Regression detection pipeline that raises an alert when: throughput drops >7% AND quality (embedding cosine / downstream eval) degrades >1% with p < 0.05 by bootstrap test
Baseline reference snapshots for FP32/FP16 for each workload and automated comparisons against INT8 and INT4 profiles
Dashboards showing tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 latency, memory usage, KV cache warm/cold differences, and quality metrics with historical trendlines
Automated PR workflow: when a quant profile change is proposed, the harness runs and annotates the PR with perf/quality deltas and a pass/fail badge
plan: Day 0: Design matrix for workloads x sequence-length x batch-size x cache-state (cold/warm)
Day 2-4: Implement load generator that replays sampled production traces and mixes synthetic tails (rare long sequences)
Day 5-8: Instrument runtime to collect per-request tokens, latency histograms, KV cache hit rate, GPU utilization and memory peaks
Day 9-11: Implement quality evaluation hooks: embedding cosine vs FP32 baseline, corpus-based ROUGE/BLEU snapshots, hallucination heuristics for instruction prompts
Day 12-14: Add statistical regression detection (bootstrap confidence intervals, paired-sample tests where applicable), define minimum detectable effect sizes
Day 15: Hook into CI/CD and nightly-run scheduler, ship dashboards and alert policies, document rollback runbook
datasets: prod-sampled-traces-2026-01 (anonymized user prompts, stratified by product area)
workloads: Long-form write: 512-4096 token generation per request
Code-generation: bursty tokens with high entropy
Summarization: long context ingestion + ~256 token output
comments: 2026-02-11 - Ava Chen: Kickoff meeting notes: align on workloads, agreed to baseline FP32/FP16 snapshots and to treat FP16 as primary production baseline for throughput comparisons.

2026-02-16 - Diego Morales: Implemented trace replayer and added sequence-length bucketing. Early runs show INT8 gains of +18% tokens/sec on short-chat but p95 latency increased by ~5% in cold-cache scenarios.

2026-02-20 - Maya Patel (QA): Added evaluation harness for embedding cosine and ROUGE snapshots. Observed INT4 introduces occasional divergence on code-gen prompts (embedding cosine dip 2.3%). Flagging for threshold discussion.
2026-02-24 - Diego Morales: Tuned batcher and kernel selection; added warmup routine to reduce cold-start tail. New runs reduce p95 delta to +1.5% for INT8 on long-form workloads.

2026-03-03 - Benji Rao (SRE): Hooked metrics into nightly Grafana dashboard and implemented bootstrap-based regression detector. Detector uses 10k bootstrap draws and reports 95% CI for mean tokens/sec and embedding_cosine.
2026-03-08 - Product Feedback (Lina Gomez): Suggested adding a pass/fail gate for PR automation: fail when throughput_loss > 7% AND embedding_cosine_loss > 0.8% to avoid noisy single-metric flips.

2026-03-10 - Diego Morales: First automated PR run attached (PR #4186). Detector flagged INT4 profile for code-gen bucket: throughput +42% but embedding cosine -2.6% with p=0.01 => requires design trade-off signoff. TBD: can we limit INT4 to non-code workloads?
notes: Statistical decisions: use paired bootstrap where the same prompts are replayed between baselines and test profiles to control input variance.
Alerting: send regression summaries to #runtime-regressions Slack with link to dashboard and a short template for triage (impact summary + suggested rollback).
Mitigation strategies: per-workload profile pinning, dynamic routing to FP16 when quality threshold fails, and automatic canarying with traffic ramp-down on failure.
Future: integrate with Optimize engine to recommend quant profiles by workload and expected P95/throughput trade-off curve.
